elements.element: Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment.
elements.evidence: Retained 7.2 still requires that "The O&M Costs ... shall be borne by the Parties in the proportions set forth in Schedule B", and the Capital Costs share under Paragraph 7 is untouched, so a mandatory spend commitment survives; the insertion only caps its duration rather than eliminating it.

elements.element: Customer pays only for usage or ordered Services.
elements.evidence: Payment remains keyed to a Schedule B proportionate share of O&M and Capital Costs, not to usage or ordered services; nothing in the rendered text ties payment to consumption.

elements.element: The commitment is limited to the current 12-month term.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence: "Teleglobe USA Inc.'s commitment to bear O&M Costs under Subparagraph 7.2 is limited to the then-current twelve (12) month period". Note: only the O&M commitment is limited; the Paragraph 7 Capital Costs share (a one-off construction contribution rather than a recurring purchase commitment) is not, which is acceptable for this element but should be confirmed.

elements.element: Customer may reduce the commitment on 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence: "...and may be reduced by Teleglobe USA Inc. on thirty (30) days' prior written notice." The right is unconditional and runs in our favour, though the permissible magnitude/floor of the reduction is left open.

elements.element: Any shortfall is handled through a true-up rather than a penalty.
elements.evidence: Subparagraph 7.7 is a one-time actual-cost settlement of Capital Costs "[a]s soon as practicable after the RFS Date" computed by the CBP; it does not address any shortfall in the (now 12-month, reducible) O&M commitment, and the drafter concedes the Paragraph 23 default remedy (reclamation of capacity) survives as a penalty-style consequence.

reasons: Fallback is incomplete: the true-up element is claimed as "already_met" by Subparagraph 7.7, but 7.7 is a Capital Costs final settlement anchored to the RFS Date and computed by the CBP — it is not a shortfall true-up for the O&M commitment the redline now makes reducible, and it does not displace the surviving default/penalty mechanic (capacity reclamation under Paragraph 23). Repair: add express operative words to the inserted sentence (or to 7.2) providing that on any reduction or shortfall Teleglobe pays only its proportionate share of O&M Costs actually incurred for the period, trued up to actual cost, and that no penalty, forfeiture, reclamation of capacity or acceleration applies in respect of the reduced amount.
Preferred level is not reached and is not claimed: the mandatory Schedule B proportionate cost-bearing obligation remains, and fees are not tied to usage or ordered services.

Secondary drafting point (not a level failure): "then-current twelve (12) month period" has no anchor in an agreement whose only defined period is the twenty-five (25) year Initial Period measured from the RFS Date; consider anchoring it to successive twelve (12) month periods commencing on the RFS Date to avoid an ambiguous temporal trigger.

Minimality holds: a single concise insertion after 7.2, no deletions, no survival tails, expense allocation, extra remedies or unrelated boilerplate, and favourable retained language (13.2/14.1 upgrade protections, 7.7 adjustments) is preserved.

Intent is preserved in substance: cross-reference to "Subparagraph 7.2" is valid, and 18.1's duration/one-year-notice mechanics, Schedule B allocation and the CBP settlement process survive without direct contradiction. Two points to tidy: the inserted text carries no subparagraph number although the margin comment calls it "7.2A", and the sentence does not say whether a reduction re-allocates the released Schedule B share to the other Parties.
